subject.title: auto-reply: /export-session lets allowed non-owners write outside the workspace

question: Should `/export-session` become owner-only, workspace-contained for authorized non-owners, or both owner-only and workspace-contained?
rationale: The outside-workspace write is a clear bug, but current docs do not explicitly say whether in-workspace HTML session export should remain available to authorized non-owner senders.

options.title: Owner-only plus contained paths
options.body: Treat session HTML exports like the sibling trajectory export and also prevent absolute or traversal paths from escaping the workspace/export area.

options.title: Contain paths only
options.body: Keep authorized non-owner session export for in-workspace outputs but reject or rewrite paths that would leave the workspace.

options.title: Private approval route
options.body: Route `/export-session` through an owner approval/private delivery flow similar to sensitive trajectory exports, at the cost of more implementation surface.

recommendation.title: Owner-only plus contained paths
recommendation.body: Treat session HTML exports like the sibling trajectory export and also prevent absolute or traversal paths from escaping the workspace/export area.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently landed the adjacent `/export-trajectory` owner-gate hardening and touched the relevant command boundary.
